titles: A · reuse the zone (zone + owned text)
B · group of anchors owns text

designs.docModel:
Reuse the existing `zone` KIND rather than add one — extend makeZone with optional content fields, keeping the wire shape a superset of today's {id,name,x,y,w,h}:
  zone { id, name, x, y, w, h, role?, content?, align?, value? }
- role: 'region' (default, today's behaviour) | 'text' | 'button' | 'input'. Absent role ⇒ legacy region, fully back-compatible.
- content: the owned string (multi-word). For role 'text'/'button' it is the body; for 'input' `content` is the label and `value` is the editable slot text.
- align: 'left' | 'center' (default 'center' for text/button, 'left' for input). Drives the text-anchor + pad.
makeText(box, content) / makeButton(box, content) / makeInput(box, label, value) are thin wrappers over makeZone that stamp role. A panel is just makeGroup over the widget-zone ids (the hull already exists) OR a parent role:'region' zone enclosing them. nextName/SELECTABLE/toJSON all already handle zone, so selection, naming, undo and persistence come for free.
designs.textAtomic:
The NEW text atomic is a "zone-content box": the resolved zone rect inset by the gutter, with text laid inside it.
- content box = the zone rect (x,y,w,h) inset by ~gutter (2px) — text never touches the rounded corner (r=14).
- baseline = the zone's vertical CENTRE (cy = y+h/2); render via dominant-baseline:central so a single-row widget's text sits on the row's cell-centre grid line. Multi-row text would stack from a top pad.
- alignment = `align` field → text-anchor:middle at cx (center) OR start at x+pad (left); pad = 12px (matches today's zone label x+10 convention).
- font = 15px monospace, theme text colour (light, e.g. #e6e9ee; accent #d6f0fc on buttons).
- width policy = FIXED-CELLS, not auto-grow. The zone owns N whole cells; text is clipped/ellipsised if it overflows the span. This is the defining tension of Approach A: text semantically wants to auto-size to its glyph run (today's pillWidth does exactly that — ~9px/char), but a zone is sized by its cell span, so the entity cannot grow to its content; the author grows it by adding cells. The 9px/char measure is retained only as an overflow check, not as the box width.
designs.spatial:
Uses the zone half-cell-offset grid: edges fall at cell BOUNDARIES (±P/2 + k·P = 30,90,150…), one rung inside via the ladder (zone ext 29 vs cell 30, 1px breathing per side). Node frames, by contrast, centre on cell CENTRES (multiples of 60). Consequences, honestly:
- Single vs multi-cell: any widget is an integer cell rectangle (1+ cols × 1+ rows). A single-cell widget is a 58px box centred on a cell centre.
- Tiling: because edges snap to boundaries, consecutive widgets ABUT cleanly with a uniform 2px gutter at each shared boundary (see the control bar: w1..w4 edges at 210/330/450). This is the grid's gift to a control bar — no manual gutter math.
- Alignment fault: a span's centre is on a grid line only for ODD cell counts. EVEN spans (e.g. the 2-cell "Export") centre on a cell BOUNDARY, so centred text lands off the cell-centre grid (the dashed guide in the mockup marks x=510, a boundary). Mixing node labels (cell-centre) with even-span widget labels (boundary) produces a half-cell horizontal misalignment that the eye catches. Mitigations: prefer odd spans for centred text, or left-align (pad from the edge, grid-independent).
designs.reuseVsNew: Maximal reuse, minimal new surface. NO new KIND — `zone` absorbs the role. Reused as-is: the zone rect render path, the half-offset span math in docToSchema/schemaToDoc, groupHull for the panel, SELECTABLE/selection/undo/toJSON, nextName. NEW (small): a `role`/`content`/`align`/`value` field set on zone; a role-aware text body in renderEl's zone branch (and the app renderer's zone branch); makeText/makeButton/makeInput wrappers. The risk of reuse is semantic, not mechanical: every existing consumer that special-cases "zone" (validation allow-list of fields, the server's unknown-field gate, anything that assumes a zone is non-interactive background) must learn that a zone can now be a foreground interactive widget. The server field gate in particular must be widened or it will reject the new fields on reload.
designs.generalization:
One primitive, four roles:
- TEXT = role:'text' — translucent zone + centred owned content. The base case.
- BUTTON = role:'button' — same zone, accent treatment (link colour #4fc3f7 fill-op 0.16, stroke-op 0.75, thicker 1.4 stroke) + centred label, signalling actionable; click = an entity event on the zone id.
- INPUT = role:'input' — a label-zone (faint) abutting a slot-zone (opaque #101010 fill, port-colour stroke) whose `value` is left-aligned with a caret; port squares on the slot edges advertise it as a first-class entity with connection sites (it can be wired into the diagram).
- PANEL / CONTROL BAR = a group (existing hull, #b388ff) — or a parent role:'region' zone — over widget-zone members laid on consecutive cells. The panel is not a special container type; it is the ordinary region+members construct already used to group nodes, now grouping widgets. That is the unification: a UI panel and a node group are the same entity, so a control bar is authored, selected, moved and persisted exactly like any diagram region.
designs.kernelOwnsText: YES — and this is the consequential shift. Today the kernel "defers labels": renderEl emits zone/node geometry with NO text, and the app renderer (app/src/renderer.js) attaches the NAME as a pill+<text> on top. Approach A moves text rendering INTO the kernel's renderEl zone branch (it now emits <text> sized/anchored from role+align+content), so headless render()/export produce labelled widgets and GRC can reason about them. The app renderer still mirrors the same output for live/incremental DOM (so input/selection/CSS keep working), but the kernel becomes the source of truth for text layout. Net: the kernel stops being label-free; it gains a typography responsibility (font, baseline, anchor, overflow) it deliberately avoided. That is defensible for first-class text but it widens the kernel's contract — worth a deliberate re-lock alongside spec.mjs.
risks: Semantic overload: 'zone' was background grouping; now it is also a foreground interactive widget. Every consumer that special-cases zone (server unknown-field gate, validation, slides export, anything assuming zones are non-interactive) must learn the new role/content/value fields or it will reject the doc on reload.

Z-order is wrong by default: DRAW_ORDER.zone=0 is back-most, behind nodes/links. A text label or button must read in FRONT of graph content; reusing the zone draw rank means widgets render under nodes. Needs a role-aware z-bump (foreground widgets) — a real exception to the clean back-to-front layering.

Fixed-cell width vs auto-grow text: the entity cannot size to its glyph run (today's pillWidth auto-grows). Authors must add cells to fit text; overflow must clip/ellipsise. This is the opposite of how a label naturally wants to behave.
Even-span centring lands off the cell-centre grid (boundary at half-offset). Centred widget text misaligns by a half-cell against node labels; only odd spans or left-align stay grid-true.
Kernel stops deferring labels: typography (font/baseline/anchor/overflow) moves into the kernel renderer, widening its contract and warranting a deliberate re-lock alongside spec.mjs.
Corner-name collision: a zone already attaches a top-left name pill. A content-owning text zone must suppress or merge that legacy label, or text appears twice.

Input is two abutting zones (label + slot) held together only by adjacency, not by a parent relation — moving one can desync the pair unless grouped; the 2px gutter between them is fixed by the ladder, not tunable.

Edit affordance / accessibility: a translucent region gives weak signal that text is editable; the value slot needs distinct treatment (done here via opaque fill + caret + ports) so users can tell text from button from input.

designs.docModel: Reuse the existing `group` KIND and add a content-type: `makeTextGroup(members, text, role)` → `{ id:'group-xxxxxx', name, members:[waypointId,...], text:'Diagram title', role:'text'|'button'|'input' }`. `text` and `role` are new optional fields on the group entity (server validate.js must whitelist them or the unknown-field gate rejects the doc). Each text entity also spawns 1–2 `waypoint` entities (`makeWaypoint(pos)`) as its anchors — they are real, persisted, occupancy-participating entities. So one "text box" = 1 group + N anchor waypoints in the document. KINDS list is unchanged; group stays non-selectable (SELECTABLE in model.mjs excludes 'group').
designs.textAtomic: The text atomic IS the group hull rect (rx = group.r = 11) acting as the content box. Text is centred in the hull: text-anchor="middle", dominant-baseline="central", at (hull.cx, hull.cy), monospace 15px, fill ~#cfd8dc. Padding = group.ext (26) on every side, i.e. the gap between the outermost anchor centre and the hull edge — NOT a text-driven inset. Width policy: FIXED-CELLS-via-anchors. The box size is (anchorCentreSpan + 52); it does NOT track the string. Auto-grow is impossible without programmatically moving the anchor waypoints, so a long string overflows the hull (visible risk: a single-anchor "Export" needs 54px but the box is only 52px). Vertical baseline is centred; there is no separate baseline/ascender model — the hull centre is the only anchor.
designs.spatial: Two grids are in play and they fight. Anchors are waypoints, which snap to CELL-CENTRES (the node/waypoint lattice, multiples of pitch). The hull then derives as centre-bbox ± 26. Because group.ext=26 ≠ half-pitch=30, the box edges land 4px INSIDE the zone half-offset grid lines — a single-cell text is 52px in a 60px cell, a 3-cell text is 172px vs the 180px zone span. So the footprint is NOT on either snap grid; it floats 4px off the half-offset boundary. Single-cell = 1 anchor → degenerate 52×52 hull centred on the cell. Multi-cell = ≥2 anchors at the corner cells. Alignment between widgets is by cell-centre placement of anchors, but the visible boxes never tile flush (8px gaps), so a control bar reads as loosely-spaced pills, not a continuous bar — hence the backing zone in the mockup to fake cohesion.
designs.reuseVsNew: Maximum reuse, zero new KIND: it leans entirely on the existing group hull (groupHull in geometry.mjs, the engine resolve group branch, the renderer group rect) and the existing waypoint entity/snap/render. New surface is tiny: two fields (`text`,`role`) on group + a server whitelist + a renderer text draw + suppressing the waypoint ring when a waypoint is an anchor. The cost of that reuse is conceptual overload: `group` now means both "hug these nodes" and "this is a labelled box", and `waypoint` means both "route bends here" and "box corner". The cheapness is real but it is borrowed against clarity.
designs.generalization: button = group{text, role:'button'} + panel fill + thicker stroke; input = a plain label text-group beside a second group{role:'input'} whose hull is the editable slot (interior slot rect inset 8/10); panel = "a group of widget-groups". This last step is where B fails: model groups contain node/waypoint ids only (groupOf/expandSelection resolve via endpointOf = node|waypoint), so a group cannot contain other groups. A panel therefore cannot BE a group-of-widgets; it degrades to a zone drawn behind loosely-placed widget-groups (exactly the mockup's control bar). So text/button/input generalise from one mechanism, but the "diagram-as-UI" recursion (panels of panels) does not — the unification stops one level short.
designs.kernelOwnsText: Yes — text rendering moves INTO the kernel for this entity. The hull is computed in the kernel (resolve/groupHull), so the natural place to draw the centred <text> is the renderer's group branch, reading el.text. That is the one genuinely attractive property of B: text lives where its box is computed, no app-side measurement. But it creates a SPLIT regime: node NAME labels stay deferred/attached in app/src/renderer.js (pill + 9px/char measuring), while group-text is kernel-owned and centred. Two text systems coexist, which undercuts the "first-class text" goal — the kernel owns SOME text, not text.
risks: Waypoint overload: anchors are real waypoints, so by default they render as routing rings (must be suppressed when group-owned) AND they register in occupancy (occupiedAnyAt/waypointAt), so a text box silently blocks routing and node placement on its anchor cells.

Derived, not declared box: hull = centre-bbox + group.ext(26). Since 26 != half-pitch 30, box edges sit 4px inside the zone half-offset grid; single-cell text = 52px in a 60px cell; widgets never tile flush (8px gaps) so a control bar isn't continuous without a faux backing zone.
No auto-grow: footprint is decoupled from string length — a long label overflows the hull (e.g. single-anchor 'Export' = 54px > 52px box). Resizing means programmatically relocating anchor waypoints.

Degenerate hull: 0 members => groupHull returns null => text vanishes; 1 member => fixed 52x52 only. The entity's existence depends on phantom anchors surviving the delete cascade (linksAt/del reconcile).

Not directly selectable: groups are excluded from SELECTABLE, so you can only select the text via an anchor waypoint (expandSelection group-as-one) — clicking the text/box selects indirectly, and the box has no native selBox path.

Panel recursion fails: model groups contain node/waypoint ids only (endpointOf), not other groups, so 'panel = group of widgets' is impossible; panels degrade to zones, so the diagram-as-UI unification stops one level short.
Doc/index bloat: every text/button/input adds 1-2 extra waypoint entities to the document and the relations/occupancy index — a control bar of 4 widgets is ~12 entities for 4 logical controls.
Split text regime: kernel owns group-text but node NAME labels remain app-side/deferred (pill, 9px/char) — two text systems, so 'first-class text' is only half-achieved.

designs.textAtomic:
The NEW text atomic = a CONTENT-BOX bound to the frame interior, NOT a free pill.
- Content box: the frame rect inset by HPAD=12 horizontally, full height vertically. Lives at resolved px (no off-grid measuring at render time — sizing already quantized upstream).
- Baseline + vertical alignment: dominant-baseline="central" anchored at the row centre cy = (r0 + (rows−1)/2)·P (single-line); multi-line stacks at 18px leading within the rows budget.
- Horizontal alignment: align→text-anchor. label/button = middle at cx; input label = start at contentBox.left; input value = middle of the slot sub-rect.
- Padding: HPAD=12 each side (interior gutter inside the 10px frame inset → text never touches the frame). VPAD implicit via central baseline.
- Width policy: FIXED-CELLS, not auto-grow. The visible box always lands on whole cells; text floats inside the quantized budget (slack absorbed by padding). This is the deliberate contrast with today's pill (which auto-grows to text px and lands off-grid). 15px monospace, fill TOKENS.text (new).
- New theme: TOKENS.text='#e8e8e8', TOKENS.textMuted='#9aa0a6', TOKENS.btnFill='#16202a', and a `.text`/`.widget` CSS block appended to KERNEL_CSS (font-family ui-monospace, font-size 15px, the role fills/strokes, .widget.selected gating).
designs.spatial: Snap: the run ANCHOR (top-left cell) snaps to the CELL-CENTRE grid (multiples of pitch) — same grid a node uses, NOT the zone half-offset grid. The box then extends right/down by whole cells, so its EDGES land on the cell-boundary (half-offset) lines exactly where zone edges land — frame inset 10px inside those, identical rhythm to a single node. Single-cell (1×1) widget is pixel-identical to a node placement (cell-centre aligned). Multi-cell: only the anchor is constrained; even-vs-odd span ambiguity is eliminated by anchoring the top-left cell rather than the geometric centre (so no half-cell drift). Alignment within a control bar: child widgets are placed on the bar's interior cell-centres, so widgets auto-align to the same column grid as the rest of the diagram — a button beside a node lines up by construction.
designs.reuseVsNew:
REUSE (unchanged): the #m-square frame template (stretched via w/h), frameR=5, the .frame CSS class + fill/stroke tokens, the frame→selection→group→zone ladder (+step=3 per rung), cellOf/cellPx/px cell math, the pillWidth text-measurement metric (9px ASCII / 15px CJK), DRAW_ORDER mechanism, renderElement/renderScene plumbing, the doc put/set/del + toJSON/load loops (just one more KIND).
NEW (additive, no edits to locked geometry): the `text` KIND + makeText/spanFor in document/model.mjs; the `texts` branch in docToSchema/schemaToDoc; a `text` resolve case in engine.mjs; a renderEl('text') case + a rectangular selBoxRect(L,w,h) generalization of selBox in renderer.mjs; bboxOf 'text' case; TOKENS.text/textMuted/btnFill + the .text/.widget CSS in theme.mjs; footprint-aware occupancy in commands.js (a multi-cell entity claims cols×rows cells).
designs.generalization:
All four are the ONE text-node atomic + a `role`:
- TEXT BOX (label): frame rendered transparent (frameOpacity 0), text-anchor middle. Pure title on cells; the frame still exists for selection/occupancy (shown faintly only when selected).
- BUTTON: same frame VISIBLE (btnFill + accent stroke TOKENS.link), centered caption, .widget gains pointer affordance class. role swaps fill/stroke only.
- INPUT: visible subtle frame, role splits the content-box into a left label region (text, start-anchored, muted) + a right SLOT sub-rect (the editable value; stroke = port green to read as a live port). Live editing later via a foreignObject/HTML overlay over the slot rect — the SVG slot is the placeholder/footprint.
- CONTROL BAR (panel): a WIDE multi-row text-node with role 'bar' = a backplane frame; its interior cells host CHILD text-nodes (title label + input + buttons). The bar is itself a diagram region (like a zone that holds nodes), and the widgets are first-class entities placed on its cells. That IS diagram-as-UI: the reconstructed top bar is just cells + widgets, authored and persisted exactly like any other diagram fragment.
designs.kernelOwnsText: YES — this is the defining architectural move of Approach C: text rendering moves INTO the kernel. Today app/src/renderer.js owns the label pill+<text> (the kernel explicitly "defers labels"); C makes `text` a resolved scene primitive emitted by engine.mjs and drawn by kernel/renderer.mjs (with the metric + tokens already sovereign in theme.mjs). Headless render()/check()/Slides export all get text for free. Scope boundary held deliberately: the NODE NAME label (an attached, decorative label on a node) STAYS app-side for now — only the new first-class TEXT entity is kernel-owned. That leaves a transitional two-owner state (app pill for node names, kernel text for text-nodes) until a later arc re-expresses the node name as an attached kernel text-node; flagged as a risk, not done here.
risks: Even-span centring: anchoring the geometric centre would put even-col boxes on a half-cell offset; mitigated by anchoring the TOP-LEFT cell-centre and growing by whole cells, but the doc x,y semantic (anchor, not centre) differs from node/zone and must be documented or callers will mis-place.

Quantized sizing vs real font metrics: cols is derived from the approximate 9px/char measure; a real monospace face that runs wider will overflow the cell budget, narrower leaves slack. Conservative HPAD=12 + ceil absorbs normal variance but CJK/emoji or a different mono face can still clip.

Two text owners during migration: node NAME labels stay app-side pills while the new text-node is kernel-owned, so two text-rendering paths coexist (divergent metrics/tokens) until the node label is re-expressed; a real but bounded inconsistency.

Multi-cell occupancy: occupiedAt/cellOf/waypointAt assume single-cell footprints; a text-node must claim cols×rows cells or it will silently overlap nodes/zones. Needs footprint-aware occupancy in commands.js + the index.

Rectangular selection geometry is new: selBox is point-symmetric (±r about origin); a generalized selBoxRect(L,w,h) tracking the ladder radius at four corners must be added and kept in lockstep with the kernel ladder.
Live INPUT editing: SVG <text> is not editable; the input slot needs a foreignObject/HTML overlay for real typing, adding a DOM seam the rest of the kernel render does not have.

Slides export parity: a multi-cell text-node must map to a Slides text box; the cell-quantized width may not round-trip cleanly against Slides inset/auto-size limits (see slides-api-constraints) — export sizing needs verification.
Scope creep into a layout engine: roles (label/button/input/bar) plus child placement edge toward a UI toolkit; without a firm atomic boundary the 'one KIND' can balloon into per-role special cases.

designs.textAtomic:
A CONTENT BOX that generalises the 26px socket: instead of a fixed glyph-socket, content is laid into the frame interior = the spanned frame inset by the cell margin. Definition (STD-derived, no magic numbers):
- Content box: x∈[frameLeft+pad, frameRight−pad], centred on the node. pad = step (3) for the inner gutter; the frame itself already keeps the locked 10px = (pitch/2 − node.ext) margin to the cell edge.
- Font: monospace 15px, advance 9px/char (reusing the app's measured 9px/char, CJK 15px) — this advance is the ONE new constant the kernel must adopt.
- Baseline: vertically centred — baseline y = cy + 5 (≈0.34em cap-centre for 15px). Glyph nodes were socket-centred; text is baseline-centred in the same box.
- Alignment: text → centre (text-anchor middle); button → centre; input → label left-anchored at content-box left, value in a nested inset slot (a second rounded content box, the editable region) right of the label, with a caret at value end.
- Width policy: FIXED-CELLS (this is the spatial-grammar-faithful choice). A widget occupies whole cells; it auto-grows by cols = ceil((textPx + 2·pad + 2·(pitch/2−node.ext)) / pitch), never sub-pitch. "Export" (54px) → 2 cells; "Diagram title" (117px) → 3 cells. Auto-grow is to the cell lattice only, so frame edges stay on the ±30 cell boundaries and selection/grouping geometry stays integer-cell. (Auto-grow-to-pixels is explicitly rejected here — it would put a node frame off the lattice and break occupancy.)
designs.spatial: Cell-centre lattice — the SAME grid as glyph nodes (centres on multiples of pitch=60), NOT the zone half-offset grid. A widget is single-cell by default; multi-cell via `span` (auto-grown by the width policy). The spanned frame is the single-cell #m-square generalised to a rounded rect of width = (spanCols−1)·pitch + 2·node.ext, height likewise — i.e. the locked 10px margin is preserved on the outer cells, identical to how a 1-cell frame sits 10px inside its 60px cell. Selection brackets (selBox) must scale from the fixed ±23 to the spanned-frame corners + step. A PANEL is a multi-cell node (its frame is the panel background plane) that hosts child widget-nodes placed on its interior cells; a group binds panel+widgets so they move as one (group-as-one already exists). Alignment within a widget is per-content (text centre, button centre, input label-left + value-slot). The control bar is widgets on consecutive single/multi cells, optionally over a panel node, all grouped — a horizontal strip of the same lattice the canvas uses.
designs.reuseVsNew: REUSE (free, no code): id namespace + KINDS/KEY/SELECTABLE, the put/set/del + undo/redo path, toJSON/load + wire format, docToSchema/schemaToDoc seam (node branch), cell snap (cellOf/gridSnap), the #m-square frame def, selBox brackets (sizing aside), group membership/expand-to-group/hull, all pointer gestures and the selection model, GRC. NEW (additive): (1) a `content` discriminator + text/label/value/span fields on node (validators + OPTIONAL entry + EXT bounds in server/validate.js — without this the unknown-field gate at validate.js line 71 rejects every widget); (2) a content switch in renderEl's node block + the text-atomic renderer (kernel acquires the 9px/char advance); (3) span-aware geometry: frame width, selBox extent, multi-cell occupancy/index keying, group-hull from footprint not centre. The net new surface is small and all of it is localised to node — there is no parallel kind ladder to build (the explicit win over Approaches A/B/C).
designs.generalization:
All four are one node with different `content`, which is the whole point:
- TEXT = node, shape:'none' (or hairline frame), content box holds centred text. The frame defers to the text.
- BUTTON = TEXT + shape:'square' + accent fill (TOKENS.link) + an `interactive` class for the click affordance/hover. Same selection brackets prove it's a node.
- INPUT = node whose content box is split: a left-anchored label + a NESTED inset content box (the value slot, the editable region) with a caret. The slot is the recursive case of the text atomic — a content box inside a content box.
- PANEL = a node that spans cells; its frame is a background plane and it HOSTS child widget-nodes (themselves nodes) on its interior cells, bound by a group.
Because every widget is a node on a cell, a CONTROL BAR is literally a row of nodes = a diagram. The toolbar and the canvas become the same editable substrate (diagram-as-UI): you draw your UI the way you draw a topology.
designs.kernelOwnsText: YES — and this is the load-bearing tradeoff of Approach D. Content text (the BODY of text/button/input/value) moves INTO the kernel: renderEl gains a text branch and the kernel must own a font metric (9px/char advance) to size content boxes and auto-grow spans. This deliberately reverses the kernel's current "defers labels" stance — but only for content text, where the text IS the entity and must be measured to be placed deterministically (the kernel is the headless/export authority; a server-side PNG/Slides export must render the widget identically, so the metric has to live in the kernel, not the DOM). The DECORATIVE attached NAME label (the pill below a glyph node, app/src/renderer.js pillWidth/NODE_LABEL_Y) can stay deferred app-side as today — it's annotation, not content. So the rule becomes: kernel owns content text (in-frame, measured, exported); app keeps the deferred name annotation. The risk is the kernel inheriting browser-divergent text metrics; mitigate by locking to the monospace 9px/char model already used app-side and treating it as spec (like pitch).
risks: Node becomes a tagged union: every `if (kind==='node')` site (renderer update(), schema, GRC, occupancy) must branch on content/span or silently mis-handle a widget. Concentrated complexity in the most central kind.

Single-cell invariants break: Model.occupiedAt/occupiedAnyAt/waypointAt and the maintained index key by ONE cell (n.x===p.x). A spanning widget/panel occupies multiple cells and would read as 'free' on its non-anchor cells — index + occupancy must become footprint-aware.

selBox is locked to ±23 (single cell) and group hull is computed from node CENTRES (groupHull). A multi-cell widget needs span-scaled brackets and a footprint-based hull; otherwise selection/grouping visuals detach from the frame.

Server gate rejects widgets until extended: validate.js (line 71 unknown-field, line 64 unknown-kind) will 400 any node carrying content/text/value/span. Must add validators + OPTIONAL entries + EXT bounds, and make `type` content-conditional, in lockstep with the model — a wire-compat change.

Kernel acquires text measurement, reversing its 'defers labels' design. Browser/headless font-metric divergence risks export mismatch; must lock the monospace 9px/char advance as spec (treat like pitch).
`type` and `shape` semantics get overloaded (type was the glyph name; shape:'none' is new). Tooling/GRC that assumes every node has a glyph type must tolerate its absence.
Link endpoints accept any node id, so a link could attach to a button/text node — semantically odd; may need a content-aware connectability rule.
Backward-compat hinges entirely on absent-content ⇒ 'glyph'; any code that writes content explicitly on legacy glyph nodes, or a default other than glyph, silently corrupts old docs.

judgment:
I've grounded the call in the actual code. Key verifications:

- **Node anchors on cell-centres** (`cellPx` = `cell·pitch`, multiples of 60); the `#m-square` frame is a centred `2·ext` square at the cell centre (`spec.mjs`, `renderer.mjs:80-82`).
- **Approach C's "stretched node" math checks out exactly**: frame inset `g = pitch/2 − node = 10`; at `cols=1`, `x = c0·P − 20, w = 40` — pixel-identical to today's node. So C reuses the frame/ladder/CSS by *sharing geometry*, not by mutating the node entity.
- **Zone anchors on the half-offset grid** and resolves at ladder ext `29` (`engine.mjs:62-65`); its edges never coincide with node-label cell-centres → Approach A's even-span drift is real, not theoretical.
- **Approach B's panel recursion provably fails**: `endpointOf` = node|waypoint only (`model.mjs:109-111`), `expandSelection` resolves groups via it, and `SELECTABLE` excludes `group` — a group cannot contain groups, so "panel = group of widgets" is impossible.
- **Kernel currently defers ALL text**: `renderer.mjs` emits zero `<text>`; every label is an app-side pill with the `9px/char` metric (`app/src/renderer.js:22,106-119`). The metric to promote to the kernel already exists.
- **The server gate is strict and additive-friendly**: unknown-field (`validate.js:71`) and unknown-kind (`:65,88`) both 400, but the `OPTIONAL` set (`:61`) is the proven absent⇒default migration trick (`node.shape`). Any new kind/field MUST land in `validate.js` (KINDS, FIELDS, OPTIONAL, SELECTABLE regex, EXT) in lockstep or reload rejects the doc.

---

## Scoring (1-5)

| Axis | A (zone) | B (group+wp) | C (text KIND) | D (node+content) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

B is eliminated outright: a derived (never declared) box off both grids, waypoint overload that pollutes occupancy/routing, panel recursion that provably fails, and a split text regime that only half-achieves "first-class text." A is eliminated for the wrong grid (half-offset), back-most z-order by default, and the eye-catching even-span misalignment against node labels — fatal for a control bar that must align with diagram content.

That leaves **C vs D**. On pure aesthetics D wins the raw sum, driven entirely by unification: one placeable thing, canvas and toolbar literally the same substrate. But that exact strength is what makes it the wrong *first* move.

## WINNER: Approach C — the new `text` KIND. (D is the north star; C is the de-risked path to it.)

The deciding factor the scoring table doesn't capture is **blast radius / parity-safety**, which the prompt explicitly demands ("first-pass", "parity-safe path"). D turns `node` — the single most-consumed, already-shipped entity — into a tagged union. Every `if (kind==='node')` site (renderer `update()`, GRC, occupancy, schema, *link-endpoint connectability*) must branch on `content`/`span` or silently mishandle a widget, and the whole migration hinges on absent-content⇒glyph holding across all of them. That is concentrated risk in the load-bearing path of a working diagram.

C gets ~90% of D's reuse via the verified "node is the degenerate 1×1 case" identity — it **shares the frame template, ladder, frameR and `.frame` CSS without overloading the node entity**. The shipped glyph-node path stays byte-for-byte (`renderEl` node branch verbatim; single-cell node occupancy unchanged). Both C and D anchor on the correct cell-centre grid, both move text into the kernel, both need footprint occupancy + a rectangular `selBox`. C buys all of that on an *isolated* kind. And critically: **once C's text atomic + footprint occupancy + rectangular selection are proven on the isolated `text` kind, you already own every mechanism D needs** — collapsing `text`-node into `node`-with-`content` later becomes a refactor with the dangerous parts already de-risked. C is not a competitor to D's unification; it is the staged, parity-safe route to it.

## What to BUILD first — the text atomic + ONE entity (`role:'label'`), parity-safe

Ship the text atomic and the label entity *alone*. Defer button/input/bar/panel to a second pass once the atomic, selection, and occupancy are proven.

Build order, each step additive (existing kinds untouched, absent-`text` docs load unchanged):

1. **Promote the font metric to spec.** Move the `9px ASCII / 15px CJK` advance from `app/src/renderer.js:pillWidth` into `kernel/theme.mjs` as the sovereign metric, and add `TOKENS.text`/`textMuted`/`btnFill` + a `.widget` CSS block. This is the one load-bearing decision — the kernel deliberately acquires a single typography constant; treat it as locked like `pitch`.
2. **Text atomic in `kernel/renderer.mjs`.** A `text` resolved primitive + `renderEl` case: content-box = frame interior inset `HPAD=12`, `dominant-baseline:central` at the row centre, `text-anchor` from `align`. Pure render — test headless via `render()`.
3. **`engine.mjs` resolve `text` case** using the verified stretched-frame math (anchor = top-left cell-centre, grow right/down by whole cells). `bboxOf` 'text' → frame rect. `DRAW_ORDER.text = 6` (front of node) — this fixes A's z-order defect by construction.
4. **`app/src/schema.js`**: `text` branch in `docToSchema`/`schemaToDoc` (anchor = top-left cell-centre; span from `cols/rows`).
5. **`document/model.mjs`**: add `'text'` to `KINDS`, `KEY` (`texts`), `SELECTABLE`; add `makeText` + `spanFor` (the quantizer: `cols = max(1, ceil((textPx + 2·HPAD + 20)/pitch))`, reusing the promoted metric).
6. **`server/validate.js` in lockstep** (the wire gate): `FIELDS.text`, add to `KINDS`, the `SELECTABLE` regex, `EXT` bounds, and the `texts` collection. Without this every widget 400s on reload — non-negotiable, lands in the same commit.
7. **Footprint-aware occupancy** in `commands.js` + the index: a multi-cell text-node claims `cols×rows` cells. Today `occupiedAt` keys one cell (`n.x===p.x`, `model.mjs:132`); a span must register all its cells or it reads "free" on non-anchor cells.
8. **`selBoxRect(w,h)`** generalizing the point-symmetric `selBox` (`renderer.mjs:11`) to track the ladder radius at four corners of a non-square frame.

Ship 1-6 to get a selectable, persistable, kernel-rendered label that lands on the node grid and exports headlessly; 7-8 complete spanning. Then **button is a one-line role** (fill/stroke swap), and **input/panel are the second entity-shape pass** (input = content-box split into a left label + a right slot sub-rect with a `foreignObject` overlay for live typing; panel/bar = a wide `role:'bar'` backplane hosting child text-nodes on its interior cells — that is the diagram-as-UI payoff).

## Grafts from the runners-up

- **From D (the convergence plan):** after the `text` atomic is proven, re-express the deferred node NAME pill (`app/src/renderer.js`) as an *attached* kernel text-node. That collapses the transitional two-owner text regime AND is the exact bridge that lets you later fold `text` into `node`-with-`content` — i.e. arrive at D's full unification with the risk already retired.
- **From A:** the input treatment — opaque slot fill + caret + port squares on the slot edges so a value field reads as a first-class, *wireable* entity with connection sites; and the abutting-tile discipline for the control bar.
- **From A/B (cautionary, already designed-in):** C's top-left-cell anchor is what *avoids* A's even-span centring drift and B's 4px float — keep the doc `x,y` semantic documented as the anchor cell (not the geometric centre), or callers will mis-place.

Files that change: `kernel/theme.mjs`, `kernel/renderer.mjs`, `kernel/engine.mjs`, `kernel/geometry.mjs` (`bboxOf`), `app/src/schema.js`, `document/model.mjs`, `server/validate.js`, `app/src/commands.js`. Locked geometry (`kernel/spec.mjs`) is untouched — C adds no rung to the ladder.
